headline: High: Open-WebUI can ingest Airflow outputs via shared files/MCP and broad egress, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can produce files and API outputs, while open-webui explicitly consumes local files, mounted volumes, MCP, and tool servers. That creates a direct content bridge where Airflow-generated text can be treated as instructions by open-webui. Because open-webui also supports MCP and browser/tool use, the interaction is dangerous by default and uncertainty should escalate.
conditions: IF Airflow writes task output into a shared file or mounted volume that open-webui reads
IF open-webui is configured to ingest MCP/tool output from Airflow-connected sources
mitigations: Disable shared file ingestion between the two systems
Route Airflow outputs through a strict JSON schema parser
Add provenance labels before open-webui displays any Airflow content
Restrict open-webui MCP/tool connectors to trusted sources only
requires-engineering: isolate the agents onto separate storage namespaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and open-webui handles files, persistent memory, API keys, and external APIs. Even though Airflow does not list sensitive data classes, open-webui’s default surfaces can move file contents and prompts to third-party services. The shared-path leakage risk is plausible in default deployments, but the evidence does not show PHI or secrets in Airflow itself.
conditions: IF Airflow task outputs contain secrets, credentials, or customer data
IF open-webui is connected to external APIs or search tools while reading shared files
mitigations: Remove secrets from Airflow task outputs
Disable external connectors in open-webui for shared-workspace sessions
Store sensitive artifacts outside any open-webui-readable directory
Rotate any API keys exposed in shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage and network egress boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow can write to shared operational state, and open-webui supports persistent shared sessions, mounted volumes, and multiple instances. Their overlapping write surfaces can conflict on shared files or artifacts even without explicit locking. The concurrency model in open-webui makes this more likely, while Airflow’s orchestration can concurrently update the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same mounted directory or artifact store
IF Airflow DAG runs and open-webui sessions modify the same file names or records
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Use file locks or transactional writes for shared artifacts
Make Airflow outputs append-only
Disable open-webui writes to the shared workspace
requires-engineering: add an orchestrator-level mutex around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can treat retrieved content, tool output, or documents as conversational context, and Airflow can generate downstream artifacts that look authoritative. If open-webui forwards Airflow-produced facts into tools or user-facing answers without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so uncertainty should be treated as dangerous.
conditions: IF open-webui uses Airflow-generated documents or logs as authoritative context
IF open-webui triggers tools or user actions based on unverified Airflow output
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Airflow-derived content
Add a verification step that checks Airflow outputs against source data
Mark Airflow outputs as untrusted in open-webui prompts
Disable auto-execution of tool calls from retrieved content
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow is a data-engineering orchestrator with broad egress, while open-webui explicitly handles files, persistent memory, API keys, and external services. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if regulated data is routed through open-webui’s storage or analytics paths. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through open-webui persistent memory or analytics
IF Airflow jobs export data into open-webui-managed files or third-party APIs
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data into open-webui
Disable analytics and persistent memory for sensitive workflows
Document retention periods for shared artifacts
Restrict API-key-bearing sessions to non-sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls per data class
